chunks: It has been narrated from the Imams, peace be upon them, that talaq al-sunnah is that when a man intends to divorce his wife, he waits until she menstruates and then becomes pure. Then he divorces her at the beginning of her waiting period, with two just witnesses, in a single sitting, and with a single utterance. If he calls one man to witness the divorce and then later calls the second, that divorce is not valid unless he makes them both witnesses together in one session.

When three periods of purity have passed for her, she has become separated from him, and he is then a suitor among the suitors. The matter rests with her: if she wishes, she marries him, and if she wishes, she does not. If he marries her after that, he marries her with a new dowry. If he then wishes to divorce her, he divorces her according to the sunnah as I have described. Whenever he divorces her with talaq al-sunnah, it is permissible for him to marry her again after that. Talaq al-sunnah is called talaq al-hadm, because when she completes her cycles and he marries her a second time, the first divorce is annulled.

Every divorce that goes against the sunnah is invalid. Whoever divorces his wife according to the sunnah may take her back so long as her waiting period has not ended. When her waiting period ends, she is separated from him and he becomes a suitor among the suitors. The testimony of women is not valid in divorce. The man who divorces according to the sunnah must provide the woman’s maintenance and lodging as long as she remains in her waiting period, and the two inherit from one another until the waiting period comes to an end.

key_terms.السُّكْنَى: the wife’s housing entitlement during the waiting period
key_terms.بِشَاهِدَيْنِ عَدْلَيْنِ: with two just witnesses whose presence is required for validity
key_terms.طَلَاقَ السُّنَّةِ: divorce performed according to the prescribed legal sunnah method
key_terms.طَلَاقَ الْهَدْمِ: a form of divorce termed annulment, where the earlier divorce is nullified after remarriage
key_terms.عِدَّتِهَا: her waiting period after divorce during which certain rulings remain in effect
key_terms.مَهْرٍ جَدِيدٍ: a new dowry required for a new marriage after separation
key_terms.نَفَقَةُ الْمَرْأَةِ: the woman’s financial maintenance owed during the waiting period

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions and legal effects of talaq al-sunnah in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This narration explains the legal form of talaq al-sunnah in Shia jurisprudence, including its conditions, witness requirements, revocability during the 'iddah, and the effects of remarriage after completion of the waiting period. It also states that any divorce contrary to this prescribed method is invalid, while affirming maintenance, housing, and mutual inheritance during the wife's 'iddah.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: It has been narrated from the Imams (peace be upon them) that talaq al-sunnah (divorce according to the prescribed method) is that when a man intends to divorce his wife, he waits until she menstruates and then becomes pure. He should then divorce her before engaging in intimacy during her waiting period, in the presence of two just witnesses, in a single sitting, and with a single utterance. If he testifies before one man and later before another, such a divorce is not valid unless both witnesses are present together in the same session.

If she completes three periods of purity, she is then separated from him, and he becomes like any other suitor.
The choice is hers - if she wishes, she may remarry him, and if she does not, she is free not to do so. If he wishes to remarry her, he must do so with a new dowry. If he later wishes to divorce her again, he must do so according to the sunnah, as described. If he divorces her in the prescribed manner, it remains permissible for him to remarry her thereafter.
This type of divorce is referred to as talaq al-hadm (divorce of annulment), meaning that if she completes her waiting period and he remarries her, the previous divorce is annulled.

Any divorce that does not conform to the prescribed sunnah is invalid.
If a man divorces his wife according to the sunnah, he has the right to take her back as long as her waiting period has not ended. Once the waiting period ends, she is separated from him, and he becomes like any other suitor.
The testimony of women alone is not acceptable in matters of divorce. The husband who divorces according to the sunnah is responsible for the financial maintenance and housing of his wife as long as she is in her waiting period. They also continue to inherit from one another until the waiting period concludes.
